name: adding-peritoneal-dialysis-program-vignette-hero
prompt: Square circular-vignette hero illustration for a clinical-operations guide, composed so the meaningful content sits inside a centred circle occupying about 88% of the canvas with a clean white margin outside it. Subject: a small Filipino dialysis-centre programme team — a nephrologist medical director, a senior PD nurse, and an administrator — standing at a planning wall in a bright modern clinic office, mapping a staged programme launch. The planning wall shows a simple vertical sequence of seven numbered cards with small diamond checkpoints between them, plus a plain floor-plan sketch of a training room and a supply store, and a simple delivery-route line to a house icon. Foreground left: a peritoneal dialysis solution bag and a coiled catheter resting on a table, rendered as restrained, medically accurate objects, not clinical close-ups. Serious clinical-operations visual language: quiet navy and slate, restrained teal accents, warm neutral daylight from a window at left, shallow depth of field, documentary rather than corporate-stock feel. Colour palette deep navy #0f1e2e, teal #1a6b72, muted gold #d4af4f accents, soft white surfaces. Calm, competent, trustworthy mood — planning, not crisis. No visible readable body text; any lettering on the wall cards must be abstract marks, not legible words. Avoid: cartoon or anime style, sci-fi holograms, neon or rainbow colours, distorted hands or extra fingers, plastic skin, AI over-sharpening, needles or blood, patient distress, infection imagery, cluttered composition, tiny unreadable text, cold clinical lighting, sensationalist design, corporate stock-photo aesthetic.

name: adding-peritoneal-dialysis-program-og
prompt: Wide editorial share-card infographic titled 'Roadmap to Adding a Peritoneal Dialysis Program'. Layout: a full-width teal header bar with the title in bold white sans-serif and a small subtitle line reading 'Seven gated phases · Freestanding or hospital-based dialysis centre'. Below it, a single horizontal sequence of seven evenly spaced rounded rectangles, numbered 0 to 7, each with a very short label — Mandate, Regulation, Operating Model, Design, Build, Validate, Launch, Scale — and a small diamond checkpoint between each pair. A restrained progression band runs beneath them from soft green through amber to deep navy. Right third: a simplified vector illustration of a peritoneal dialysis solution bag and catheter beside a small house icon connected by a dotted delivery line, in muted teal-blue tones. Bottom: a full-width teal footer banner with a single takeaway line 'Opening means the programme can support the patient at home — not that space, staff and supplies exist.' Clean panel-grid infographic style on a soft white background, flat vector, no directional lighting, generous whitespace, bold readable sans-serif typography with clear hierarchy, no small text. Colour palette deep navy #0f1e2e, teal #1a6b72, gold #d4af4f, soft white panels. Calm, authoritative, educational. Avoid: cartoon appearance, 3D bevels, drop shadows, neon or rainbow gradients, cluttered density, tiny unreadable text, sci-fi interfaces, stock-photo aesthetic, fear-inducing imagery, medical photographs of patients.

name: adding-peritoneal-dialysis-program-01-fsdc-vs-hbdc
prompt: Clean two-column comparison infographic on a soft white background, titled 'Freestanding vs hospital-based dialysis centre — the same ten domains, two failure patterns'. Left column header bar in teal reads 'FSDC · Freestanding dialysis centre'; right column header bar in deep navy reads 'HBDC · Hospital-based dialysis centre'. Between the two columns runs a narrow vertical spine listing ten domain labels aligned as shared rows: Governance, Regulation, Acute care, Catheter access, Microbiology, Pharmacy, Backup HD, Training, Logistics, Quality. Each side of every row carries a very short phrase and a small monoline icon — the left side emphasising signed external agreements, transport and couriers; the right side emphasising named internal owners, protected scheduling and validated service levels. A slim caption band at the bottom in teal reads 'Signed agreement = designed. Tested tracer case = validated.' Flat vector panel-grid style, no lighting, generous spacing, bold sans-serif labels with clear hierarchy, no paragraphs of small text. Colour palette deep navy #0f1e2e, teal #1a6b72, muted gold #d4af4f accents, soft white and pale grey panel fills. Calm, organised, educational. Avoid: cartoon style, 3D effects, neon or rainbow colours, uneven grid, mismatched panel sizes, cluttered density, tiny unreadable text, photographs, hospital branding or real logos.

name: adding-peritoneal-dialysis-program-02-phase-gate-roadmap
prompt: Clinical-algorithm style flowchart on a white background, in the visual language of a resuscitation or guideline algorithm, titled 'Phase-gate roadmap — a critical finding blocks launch regardless of the overall score'. Vertical flow from top to bottom with eight navy rounded action rectangles labelled in order: Phase 0 Mandate and baseline, Phase 1 Regulation and payment, Phase 2 Operating model, Phase 3 Detailed design, Phase 4 Build and contract, Phase 5 Validate, Phase 6 Controlled launch, Phase 7 Stabilise and scale. Between each pair of phases sits a teal diamond decision node labelled 'Gate — go / conditional go / no go', with a red return arrow curving back up to the preceding phase on a no-go branch. Two amber warning branches leave the diagram at the side, one from Phase 0 labelled 'Stop conditions' and one from Phase 5 labelled 'Critical finding — do not launch'. A short legend panel in the lower right defines the three finding severities using both an icon and a colour: critical, major, improvement. Flat vector, clean thin connector lines with clear arrowheads, generous spacing, bold readable sans-serif labels, no small print. Colour palette deep navy #0f1e2e action boxes, teal #1a6b72 decision diamonds, restrained amber for warnings, restrained clinical red for stop nodes, white background. Calm, authoritative, unambiguous. Avoid: cartoon style, 3D effects, drop shadows, neon or rainbow gradients, crossing or tangled connectors, tiny unreadable text, decorative medical imagery, photographs.

name: adding-peritoneal-dialysis-program-03-supply-chain
prompt: Clean process-flow infographic on a soft white background, titled 'The PD supply chain is a clinical safety system'. A single wide horizontal chain of nine linked rounded nodes runs left to right, each with a small monoline icon: Authorised prescription, Forecast and order, Supplier allocation, Receiving and inspection, Controlled storage, Patient-specific pick, Protected transport, Home delivery and acceptance, Home inventory reconciliation. A curved return arc loops from the last node back beneath the chain to a final node group labelled Returns, Quarantine, Recall, Waste. Above the chain, four teal control-point markers drop onto Receiving, Storage, Picking and Delivery, each with a two-word label — lot capture, environment check, dual verification, identity-safe handover. Below the chain runs a slim amber risk band naming what each control prevents: wrong lot, temperature excursion, failed delivery, address disclosure, untraceable recall. Right edge shows a small simplified house icon with stacked solution boxes inside. Flat vector panel style, no lighting, generous whitespace, bold readable sans-serif labels with clear hierarchy, no dense paragraphs. Colour palette deep navy #0f1e2e, teal #1a6b72, muted gold #d4af4f, restrained amber, soft white and pale grey fills. Calm, systematic, educational. Avoid: cartoon style, 3D boxes, drop shadows, neon or rainbow colours, tangled arrows, cluttered density, tiny unreadable text, delivery-company branding or real logos, photographs.
